title: Neckbeard – a DevOps/platform/SRE plugin for your agent
title_zh: Neckbeard – 适用于您智能体的 DevOps/平台/SRE 插件

paragraphs.en: Agent plugin that scaffolds tested, cost-honest cloud infrastructure from a versioned module catalog
paragraphs.zh: 用于从版本化模块目录搭建经过测试、成本透明的云基础设施的智能体插件

paragraphs.en: A plugin for your coding agent that turns an app into cloud infrastructure you can actually review, with the monthly bill attached.
paragraphs.zh: 一个面向你的编码智能体的插件，它能把一个应用变成你真正可以审查的云基础设施，并附上每月账单。

paragraphs.en: Coding agents are great at application code and weirdly confident about infrastructure. Ask one to "deploy this to AWS" and you'll get three hundred lines of plausible HCL, a security group open to the world, an IAM policy with a star in it, and no idea what any of it costs. It reads like the work of someone who has absorbed every blog post and never once been paged. The model isn't lying to you. It has simply never seen the invoice.
paragraphs.zh: 编码智能体擅长应用代码，却对基础设施有着莫名其妙的自信。 让它「把这个部署到 AWS」，你会得到三百行看起来挺像样的 HCL、一个对全世界开放的安全组、一个带星号的 IAM 策略，以及完全不知道这一切要花多少钱。 读起来就像出自一个读过所有博客文章、却从没在深夜被故障告警叫醒过的人之手。 模型并没有骗你。 它只是从没见过账单而已。

paragraphs.en: neckbeard splits the job. Humans maintain a catalog of OpenTofu modules that are versioned, tested in CI on every change, and scoped to one honest workload shape: a container image, up to ten HTTP, worker, and cron processes, Postgres, object storage, secrets. The agent reads your repo, works out what the app needs, asks you the questions code can't answer, and maps the answers onto catalog inputs. Everything in between is deterministic Go. The planner writes a hash-verified blueprint.yaml , the renderer is a pure function of it, and regeneration refuses to overwrite a file you've touched. The agent never invents infrastructure. If your app needs Redis, you get a named finding that says the catalog doesn't do Redis yet, rather than a module that looks like it might.
paragraphs.zh: neckbeard 负责拆分任务。 人类维护一个 OpenTofu 模块目录，这些模块有版本控制、在 CI 中对每次变更进行测试，并且范围限定在一种诚实的工作负载形态：一个容器镜像、最多十个 HTTP、worker 和 cron 进程、Postgres、对象存储、密钥。 智能体会读取你的代码仓库，弄清楚应用需要什么，向你提出代码无法回答的问题，并把答案映射到目录输入上。 中间的所有环节都是确定性的 Go 代码。 规划器写出经过哈希校验的 blueprint.yaml，渲染器是它的纯函数，而重新生成时会拒绝覆盖你修改过的文件。 智能体从不凭空发明基础设施。 如果你的应用需要 Redis，你会得到一条明确的发现，说明目录尚不支持 Redis，而不是一个看起来似乎可行的模块。

sents.en: neckbeard splits the job.
sents.zh: neckbeard 负责拆分任务。

paragraphs.en: It covers AWS, GCP, and Azure, with GitHub Actions or GitLab CI, as serverless containers (Cloud Run, ECS Fargate, Container Apps) or Kubernetes (EKS, GKE, AKS). The plugin shape is borrowed from ponytail , which proved a plugin can be mostly one good prompt.
paragraphs.zh: 它涵盖 AWS、GCP 和 Azure，配合 GitHub Actions 或 GitLab CI，可作为无服务器容器（Cloud Run、ECS Fargate、Container Apps）或 Kubernetes（EKS、GKE、AKS）部署。 该插件的设计形态借鉴了 ponytail，后者证明了一个插件可以主要就是一段好的提示词。

sents.en: It covers AWS, GCP, and Azure, with GitHub Actions or GitLab CI, as serverless containers (Cloud Run, ECS Fargate, Container Apps) or Kubernetes (EKS, GKE, AKS).
sents.zh: 它涵盖 AWS、GCP 和 Azure，配合 GitHub Actions 或 GitLab CI，可作为无服务器容器（Cloud Run、ECS Fargate、Container Apps）或 Kubernetes（EKS、GKE、AKS）部署。

sents.en: The plugin shape is borrowed from ponytail , which proved a plugin can be mostly one good prompt.
sents.zh: 该插件的设计形态借鉴了 ponytail，后者证明了一个插件可以主要就是一段好的提示词。

paragraphs.en: /plugin marketplace add bealesh/neckbeard /plugin install neckbeard@neckbeard Then open your app's repo and run /neckbeard:analyze . Your first neckbeard command installs the small CLI the plugin drives (a sha256-verified release binary, or go install if you have Go around), and that's the whole setup. Cost estimates and validation lean on tools you may already have, namely Infracost, OpenTofu, and Checkov. /neckbeard:doctor tells you what's missing and what each one buys you.
paragraphs.zh: /plugin marketplace add bealesh/neckbeard /plugin install neckbeard@neckbeard 然后打开你的应用仓库并运行 /neckbeard:analyze 。 你的第一个 neckbeard 命令会安装该智能体（agent）插件所驱动的小型 CLI（一个经 sha256 校验的发布二进制文件，或者如果你有 Go 环境则通过 go install 安装），这就是全部的设置。 成本估算和验证依赖于你可能已有的工具，即 Infracost、OpenTofu 和 Checkov。/neckbeard:doctor 会告诉你缺少什么，以及每个工具能带来什么好处。

paragraphs.en: Codex, Cursor, or anything else that reads a SKILL.md : see INSTALL.md .
paragraphs.zh: Codex、Cursor 或任何读取 SKILL.md 的工具：请参见 INSTALL.md。

paragraphs.en: You run /neckbeard:analyze and the agent reads the repo the way a careful new hire would. Dockerfiles, exposed ports, environment variables, health endpoints, the Procfile, the corner of settings.py where Django quietly reads DATABASE_URL . It writes an app profile in which every fact carries a file and line number, every inference carries a confidence, and every assumption is loud. Then it asks you the things it genuinely can't know: how much traffic to expect, how much downtime you'll tolerate, whether that Postgres is one you already run or one you want built, what the worker is for. Your answers get recorded next to the assumptions they resolve, and planning refuses to run while any of them is still open.
paragraphs.zh: 你运行 /neckbeard:analyze，智能体会像一个谨慎的新员工那样阅读这个仓库。 Dockerfile、暴露的端口、环境变量、健康检查端点、Procfile，还有 settings.py 里 Django 悄悄读取 DATABASE_URL 的那个角落。 它会写一份应用画像，其中每一条事实都带有文件名和行号，每一条推断都带有置信度，每一个假设都标得清清楚楚。 然后它会问那些它确实无法知道的事情：预期多少流量、能容忍多长的停机时间、那个 Postgres 是你已经在用的还是希望新建的、那个 worker 是做什么用的。 你的回答会被记录在它们所解决的假设旁边，而只要有任何一个假设仍未解决，规划就无法运行。

paragraphs.en: /neckbeard:estimate plans against the catalog and shows you the bill before anything exists. /neckbeard:sync scaffolds the infrastructure, the pipelines, and on Kubernetes the cluster manifests, then validates them and tells you precisely what it did and didn't prove. From there you review the files like any other pull request and follow the generated docs/bootstrap.md once per environment, with real credentials in your own hands. The agent never gets those.
paragraphs.zh: /neckbeard:estimate 在任何资源创建之前，针对目录进行规划评估并展示账单。/neckbeard:sync 会搭建基础设施、流水线，以及在 Kubernetes 上生成集群清单，然后对其进行验证，并准确告诉你它证明和不证明了什么。 之后，你可以像审查其他任何拉取请求一样审查这些文件，并按照生成的 docs/bootstrap.md 在每个环境中执行一次，真实凭据始终掌握在你自己手中。 智能体永远拿不到这些凭据。

paragraphs.en: neckbeard disco -project myapp One image, one HTTP service, optional workers and cron jobs, and Postgres on the server (or connections to existing services). You supply and operate the server, including backups. This path has no cost estimate, spending ceiling, or cloud validation integration. Existing outputs are refused unless you use -force , which replaces both files, including edits. See the Disco reference for scope and test evidence.
paragraphs.zh: neckbeard disco -project myapp：一个镜像、一个 HTTP 服务、可选的 worker 与 cron 任务，以及服务器上的 Postgres（或连接到现有服务）。 由你提供并运维服务器，包括备份。 此路径没有成本估算、支出上限或云验证集成。 除非使用 -force，否则已存在的输出会被拒绝；-force 会替换两个文件，包括其中的编辑内容。 有关范围和测试证据，请参阅 Disco 参考文档。

paragraphs.en: The asterisk matters. Infracost can't price Container Apps compute yet, and the honest move is to say so rather than let a low number lie, so the report lists every resource it couldn't price right next to the total. The rest is what you'd want from anyone who has read a cloud bill with their name on it: the idle baseline separated from usage, the usage assumptions written down where you can edit them, low, expected, and high scenarios, and a footer saying where the numbers came from. The table is also how the tool argues. When a solo developer asks for Kubernetes, the numbers say "not yet" so nobody else has to.
paragraphs.zh: 星号很重要。 Infracost 还无法为 Container Apps 的计算资源定价，而诚实的做法是明说这一点，而不是让一个偏低的数字撒谎，因此报告把每一个无法定价的资源都列在总额旁边。 其余部分正是任何一个认真读过自己名下云账单的人所想要的：空闲基线与用量分开列出、用量假设写在你可以修改的地方、低、预期和高三种场景，以及一个注明数字来源的页脚。 这张表也是工具表达观点的方式。 当一个独立开发者提出想要 Kubernetes 时，这些数字会替所有人说出“现在还不行”，不必别人再费口舌。

paragraphs.en: Infrastructure tooling has a long tradition of implying more than it has proven. A passing tofu validate has never once meant a thing deploys. neckbeard reports in three levels and insists on showing you the third:
paragraphs.zh: 基础设施工具有着悠久的历史传统：言过其实，超过其实际验证过的程度。 一条通过验证的 tofu validate 从来都不代表有东西真的部署了。neckbeard 报告三个层级的内容，并坚持要给你展示第三个层级：

sents.en: Infrastructure tooling has a long tradition of implying more than it has proven.
sents.zh: 基础设施工具有着悠久的历史传统：言过其实，超过其实际验证过的程度。

sents.en: A passing tofu validate has never once meant a thing deploys. neckbeard reports in three levels and insists on showing you the third:
sents.zh: 一条通过验证的 tofu validate 从来都不代表有东西真的部署了。neckbeard 报告三个层级的内容，并坚持要给你展示第三个层级：

paragraphs.en: V0 PASSED tofu validate [prd] V0 PASSED checkov policy [prd] every skip carries a written reason V0 PASSED kubeconform (clusters/) V1 NOT EXERCISED authenticated plan requires cloud credentials V2 NOT EXERCISED deployment verification requires cloud credentials V0 is syntax and policy. Every Checkov skip in the generated config carries a written reason, because a skip without one is a lie about your security posture. V1 is an authenticated plan and V2 is a verified deployment; both need credentials, and both stay NOT EXERCISED until a human runs them. When live runs break, the failures go into the public findings ledger and from there into the catalog. The first real deployment produced ten of them, and five became module fixes the same afternoon. Degraded paths say why: an Azure plus GitLab merge-request plan can't federate, so the generated pipeline says that out loud instead of failing in a way you'd lose an evening to.

paragraphs.en: Three isolated environments with their own state, sized by tier presets that spell out traffic, availability, recovery objectives, and how many people are actually around to operate the thing. Every preset value is visible and overridable within the catalog's tested envelope, and anything outside that envelope is marked rather than blessed. Pipelines come from one internal model for either CI: test, build, scan (Trivy blocks HIGH and CRITICAL), push, plans on pull requests under a read-only identity, applies on main under a write identity, production gated behind environment protection. There are no static cloud keys anywhere. It's OIDC federation end to end, and a test fails the build if a rendered pipeline so much as mentions AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY . Networks are private by default, secret managers hold the names the operator fills in (values never pass through neckbeard, its state, or your git history), and managed WAF rules switch on where the tier calls for them. Money gets two controls that are never confused with each other: monthly_budget_alert renders a real cloud budget per environment that notifies people, and monthly_ceiling is the one that actually refuses, enforced at the only point a limit can be enforced, before the resources exist.
paragraphs.zh: 三个相互隔离的环境，各自拥有独立状态，其规模由分层预设决定，这些预设明确规定了流量、可用性、恢复目标，以及实际有多少人来运维这套东西。 每个预设值都可见，并且可以在目录经过测试的范围内进行覆盖，超出该范围的任何配置都会被标记出来，而不是被放行。 流水线来自统一的内部模型，无论哪种 CI 都是：测试、构建、扫描（Trivy 会阻断 HIGH 和 CRITICAL 级别）、推送、在拉取请求上以只读身份执行计划、在 main 分支上以写入身份执行应用，生产环境则由环境保护机制把关。 任何地方都不存在静态云密钥。 全程采用 OIDC 联合认证，只要渲染出的流水线中哪怕提到 AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY，一个测试就会使构建失败。 网络默认私有，密钥管理器保存运维人员填写的名称（实际值绝不会经过 neckbeard、其状态或你的 git 历史），托管 WAF 规则会在分层配置要求的地方启用。 资金有两项互不混淆的控制：monthly_budget_alert 为每个环境渲染真实的云预算并通知相关人员，而 monthly_ceiling 才是真正会拒绝的那个，它只在限制能够被执行的唯一时间点生效——即资源尚不存在之时。

paragraphs.en: Pre-alpha, and specific about which parts.

paragraphs.en: The plugin's product today is the front half: reviewable infrastructure, pipelines, a cost estimate, and a runbook you can hand to whoever holds the credentials. The deployment lifecycle underneath it ( neckbeard release , documented in the skill) exists and has worked for real on two lanes, but it stays experimental until it clears the gates in the launch plan . Static validation is not deployment proof. Landing zones, meaning org structure and guardrails, the Path F story in DESIGN.md , are designed and not built.
paragraphs.zh: 该插件目前的产品是前半部分：可审查的基础设施、流水线、成本估算，以及一份可以交给持有凭据之人的运行手册。 其底层的部署生命周期（neckbeard release，已在 skill 中记录）已经存在，并在两条路径上真正运行过，但在通过 launch plan 中的各项关卡之前，它仍保持实验状态。 静态验证不等于部署证明。 着陆区，即组织结构和防护栏，也就是 DESIGN.md 中的 Path F 方案，目前只有设计而尚未构建。
